page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores. Powered by Intel Xeon 8259CL processors operating at a 3.1 GHz base frequency on the x86_64 architecture, the system provides 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Hardware resources include 3600 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage and 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on raw hardware without hypervisor virtualization overhead, the system supports hardware-level instruction extensions including AVX-512, AES cryptography, and Intel VMX virtualization.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high throughput across multi-threaded computational and memory workloads. The instance achieved top-quartile performance in multi-core processing with a stress-ng score of 82018.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 58133.28. The memory subsystem recorded 224.19 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 97.97 GB/sec for sequential writes. Operational benchmarks show strong throughput in data processing, recording 76.05 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, 22158.48 on PassMark database operations, and 48.73 GB/sec in static web serving. Single-core metrics in Geekbench and stress-ng placed within median industry brackets.

The primary tradeoff of this platform centers on compute acceleration; the lack of dedicated GPUs results in lower relative efficiency for large language model inference and text generation. Qualitative cost efficiency is defined by the high physical consolidation of resources, integrating massive RAM capacity, direct NVMe storage, and high-bandwidth networking onto a single non-virtualized machine. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory caches, high-concurrency relational database engines, large-scale ETL pipelines, and low-latency data processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon 8259CL cores clocked at 3.1 GHz. The platform is configured with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 3600 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage, and 100 Gbps baseline networking without hypervisor virtualization overhead. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-tier multi-threaded compute and data throughput, reaching 76.05 million Redis SET operations per second and 224.19 GB/sec in uncached memory read bandwidth, while single-core performance remains at standard median levels. The absence of hardware accelerators makes it inefficient for deep learning generation tasks, but its high memory density and local storage provide balanced performance for large in-memory databases, transaction-heavy relational databases, real-time analytics, and enterprise data processing workloads.
